text.content:
Source: Sabbat Guide

The Sabbat, who name themselves the Sword of Caine, are the vampires of the Great Jyhad: a holy war against the Antediluvians, the ancient and monstrous progenitors of the clans, and against the Camarilla, whom the Sabbat brand as the Antediluvians' unwitting servants. The sect was born out of the Anarch Revolt, when rebellious neonates of Clans Lasombra and Tzimisce destroyed their own Antediluvians and shattered the old elder-dominated order. Rather than accept the peace of the Convention of Thorns that followed, these anarchs chose endless war instead, convinced that the only way to escape the fate of being drained or devoured by their monstrous forebears at Gehenna is to strike first and never stop striking. Where the Camarilla clings to the Masquerade and the pretense of humanity, the Sabbat has embraced its damnation. Its members consider themselves already lost to the Beast, and rather than mourn their humanity, they flaunt their monstrosity as a mark of freedom.

The sect is led rather than ruled, and its hierarchy is loose and often resented by the young Cainites who do most of its fighting. At the base of Sabbat society is the pack, a tight surrogate family of vampires bound to one another through shared ritual; a Sabbat vampire belongs to only one pack at a time, usually the one that performed her Creation Rites. Each pack is led by a Ductus, whose authority may come from brute dominance, ritual combat, or genuine respect, and who handles the pack's day-to-day and logistical decisions. Alongside the Ductus stands the pack's Priest, its spiritual leader, who administers rites such as the Vaulderie and oversees the pack's religious observances. Above individual packs, a Bishop maintains Sabbat influence within a city, sometimes compared to a Camarilla primogen, while an Archbishop rules an entire city outright and also serves as its spiritual authority. Cardinals oversee whole territories and the archbishops within them, and at the very top sits the Regent, the sect's sole recognized leader, of whom only one exists at any time. Templars occupy a position outside this chain of command entirely, acting as impartial enforcers of Sabbat law answerable to their specific duties rather than to local politics.

No practice binds the Sabbat together more than the Vaulderie: the mingled blood of every vampire in a pack, consecrated by the pack priest and drunk by all members together. It creates a vinculum, an artificial blood tie of loyalty between packmates, and is performed again and again - before battle, after crisis, or simply as nightly ritual - to keep a pack unified. New members are brought into the sect through the Creation Rites, in which a priest brands the initiate's forehead with a flaming brand while she swears an oath of loyalty to her pack, its chain of command, and the Sabbat itself; the rite is capped with a Vaulderie shared among the new packmates.

Culturally, the Sabbat prizes violence, zealotry, and pack loyalty above all else, and its members reject the Road of Humanity in favor of the various Paths of Enlightenment - inhuman codes such as the Path of Caine, the Path of the Feral Heart, and the Path of Honorable Accord - each of which exalts some aspect of vampiric nature rather than clinging to a lost mortality. This is a sect that treats its own dissolution as unthinkable even as corruption and infighting eat at it from within, one where elders often manipulate zealous neonates into fighting the Jyhad in their place. Distinctive rites mark its calendar and its justice alike: the War Party pits packs against one another to hunt and diablerize an elder Kindred for glory and status, while the Wild Hunt turns the Vaulderie and fire against traitors within the sect's own ranks.
